For reciprocal validation supply a finite partition of [δ,1] with exact algebraic endpoints and nonnegative Bernstein coefficients on each cell for the polynomials εx+(xp(x)−δ/2) and εx−(xp(x)−δ/2). Check endpoints cover the interval without gaps, and verify each coefficient expansion by exact finite polynomial arithmetic. Nonnegative Bernstein basis functions sum to one, so these checks prove |xp(x)−δ/2|≤εx, hence the desired reciprocal bound since x≥δ>0. The phase-list/complement polynomial identity certifies global boundedness. Coefficient-generation, partition construction and exact algebraic bit costs remain separate; a strict ε/2 approximation leaves a positive margin for finite Bernstein subdivision. All validation loops are over supplied finite lists.
